claims.text: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial FCC/B2 lamellar material exhibits strong-yet-brittle behavior.
The initial FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent and prone to interfacial cracking.
HPHT treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will transform the FCC/B2 lamellae into a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
The HPHT-induced hierarchical microstructure will contain coherent interfaces.
Coherent interfaces facilitate preferential dislocation transfer from the ductile FCC phase to the harder B2 phase.
Dislocation transfer across coherent FCC/B2 interfaces relieves stress concentrations.
Relief of interfacial stress concentrations produces a more homogeneous strain distribution.
The hierarchical microstructure promotes the activation of dislocations, stacking faults, microbands, and twins.
The specified HPHT treatment will increase strength to approximately 1150 MPa.
The specified HPHT treatment will increase room-temperature tensile ductility to approximately 36%.
The treatment will shift fracture from catastrophic interfacial cracking to distributed microcracking.
Conventionally arc-melted and cast eutectic high-entropy alloys exhibit room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility.
The beneficial effects are expected only at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours because these parameters induce the hierarchical microstructure.
Conventional hot isostatic pressing or lower-pressure thermomechanical treatments will not yield the same improvements.
